note: Demo rule set. All values are verified:false until checked against the official text (see VERIFY.md). Rule texts are paraphrases unless text_status says otherwise.

rules.source: SOLAS II-2/13 + FSS Code Ch. 13 (means of escape)
rules.clause: Corridor clear width (clause to verify)
rules.text: Corridors forming part of the means of escape shall have a clear width of not less than 900 mm.

rules.source: SOLAS II-2/13 + FSS Code Ch. 13 (means of escape)
rules.clause: Stairway clear width (clause to verify)
rules.text: Stairways shall have a clear width of not less than 900 mm (more depending on the number of persons).

rules.source: SOLAS II-2/13 (means of escape)
rules.clause: Two means of escape from each accommodation section: 13.3 passenger ships / 13.4 cargo ships (clause to verify)
rules.text: At least two widely separated means of escape shall be provided from each section or zone of accommodation and service spaces.

rules.source: SOLAS II-2/13 (means of escape)
rules.clause: Means of escape from machinery spaces of category A (clause to verify)
rules.text: Two means of escape shall be provided from each machinery space of category A; one of them may be a protected escape trunk.

rules.source: SOLAS II-2/13 (means of escape, passenger ships)
rules.clause: Dead-end corridors, passenger ships (clause to verify)
rules.text: Dead-end corridors exceeding 13 m in length shall not be permitted (passenger ships).

rules.source: SOLAS II-2/13 (means of escape, cargo ships)
rules.clause: Dead-end corridors, cargo and special purpose ships (clause to verify)
rules.text: Dead-end corridors having a length of more than 7 m shall not be permitted (cargo ships; applied to research vessels under the SPS Code).

rules.source: ADA 2010 Standards / PVAG
rules.clause: 403.5.1 Clear width of walking surfaces
rules.text: The clear width of walking surfaces on an accessible route shall be 36 inches (915 mm) minimum.

rules.source: ADA 2010 Standards / PVAG
rules.clause: 404.2.3 Door clear width
rules.text: Door openings on an accessible route shall provide a clear width of 32 inches (815 mm) minimum.

rules.source: ADA 2010 Standards / PVAG
rules.clause: 405.2 Ramp slope
rules.text: Ramp runs shall have a running slope not steeper than 1:12.

rules.source: IGF Code (gas-fuelled ships) - simplified for demo
rules.clause: Fuel tank location (simplified, to verify)
rules.text: LNG fuel tanks shall be separated from passenger spaces (simplified demo rule).
rules.basis_note: Not a literal IGF clause. Mentor guidance: LNG tanks must sit fully outside passenger areas for safety reasons (unwritten design practice).

rules.source: IGF Code (gas-fuelled ships)
rules.clause: 5.3.3 Fuel tank distance from the ship side (clause to verify; simplified to the deck plan)
rules.text: Fuel storage tanks shall be located not less than B/5 or 11.5 m, whichever is less, from the ship side, measured inboard at right angles to the centreline.

rules.source: International Convention on Load Lines 1966, Annex I
rules.clause: Regulation 12 - Doors (sill height, to verify)
rules.text: The height of the sills of doorways in bulkheads at the ends of enclosed superstructures shall be at least 380 mm above the deck.

rules.source: International Convention on Load Lines 1966, Annex I
rules.clause: Regulation 25 - Protection of the crew (guard rail height, to verify)
rules.text: Efficient guard rails or bulwarks shall be fitted on all exposed parts of the freeboard and superstructure decks; their height shall be at least 1 m from the deck.

rules.source: DNV Rules for Classification of Ships (class rule example)
rules.clause: Hull equipment - bulwarks and guard rails, minimum height (part/chapter/section to verify)
rules.text: Bulwarks or guard rails on exposed decks shall have a height of at least 1.0 m above the deck.

rules.source: MARPOL Annex I
rules.clause: Regulation 12 - Tanks for oil residues (sludge), to verify
rules.text: Every ship of 400 gross tonnage and above shall be provided with a tank or tanks of adequate capacity to receive the oil residues (sludge).

rules.source: IACS UR W11 (Rev.9): Normal and higher strength hull structural steels
rules.clause: W11 1.1, 1.3, 1.4; grade designations in the chemical composition table, note 1 ("H" may be added)
rules.text: 1.1 These requirements apply to weldable normal and higher strength hot-rolled steel plates, wide flats, sections and bars intended for use in hull construction. 1.3 Provision is made for four grades of normal strength steel based on the impact test requirements. For higher strength steels provision is made for three strength levels (315, 355 and 390 N/mm2) each subdivided into four grades based on the impact test temperature. 1.4 Steels differing in chemical composition, deoxidation practice, conditions of supply and mechanical properties may be accepted, subject to the special approval of the Classification Society.
rules.text_note: Extracted from the IACS PDF (mirror copy); compare with the copy on iacs.org.uk before setting verified.
rules.basis_note: UR W11 defines the hull structural steel grades. That hull structure (SWBS 1xx) must use one of them, unless specially approved, is ShipCheck's reading of class practice. Aluminium, stainless steel and non-structural materials are listed as not applicable.
rules.else_explanation: It is not a UR W11 hull structural steel grade, so it may only be used with the special approval of the Classification Society (UR W11 1.4). Add the approval reference to the model or change the material.

rules.source: IACS UR S6 (Rev.9): Use of steel grades for various hull members, ships of 90 m in length and above
rules.clause: S6.1, Table 7 (material grade by thickness and class); Table 1 (material class of the member)
rules.text: Materials in the various strength members are not to be of lower grade than those corresponding to the material classes and grades specified in Table 1 to Table 7. [...] The material grade requirements for hull members of each class depending on the thickness are defined in Table 7. For strength members not mentioned in Tables 1 to 6, Grade A/AH may generally be used. The steel grade is to correspond to the as-built plate thickness and material class.
rules.text_note: Extracted from the IACS PDF (mirror copy); compare with the copy on iacs.org.uk before setting verified.
rules.basis_note: UR S6 is written for ships of 90 m and above; the RCRV is about 60 m. Applied as the closest published IACS table until the DNV requirement for vessels under 90 m is identified (VERIFY.md). Only shell (SWBS 110), bulkheads (120) and decks (130) are checked: the members Table 1 names.
rules.column_hint: UR S6 Table 1: member category, and position within 0.4L / 0.6L amidships
rules.unknown_column_note: UR S6 Table 1 still allows Grade A/AH for secondary and primary members outside 0.4L amidships, and the position is not in the model.

rules.source: DNV rules: minimum plate thickness (value not yet in the project)
rules.clause: Not yet identified (minimum thickness per structural member)
rules.text: Minimum plate thickness per structural member group. No official value is in the project yet.
rules.draft_reason: No official minimum thickness per structural group is available in the project (class rules give formulas in ship length and member location, e.g. bottom, side, deck). The value is left empty instead of guessed. Closest check the data supports: every plate has a parsed thickness (DQ-DESIGN-STATUS / steel grade checks report missing values).

rules.source: IGC Code 3.5.3.1.2 (as quoted in IACS UI GC16); same figure in 46 CFR 154.340
rules.clause: 3.5.3.1.2 (access through horizontal openings, hatches or manholes)
rules.text: For access through horizontal openings, hatches or manholes, the minimum clear opening shall be not less than 600 mm x 600 mm.
rules.basis_note: Written for gas carriers. Used here as the reference minimum for a hatch a person wearing breathing apparatus can pass. The rule that applies to escape hatches on the RCRV is a mentor question (VERIFY.md). Round manholes are not checked.

rules.source: SOLAS Chapter II-2, Regulation 4 (probability of ignition)
rules.clause: II-2/4.2.2.5.1 (oil fuel pipes, valves and fittings)
rules.text: Oil fuel pipes and their valves and fittings shall be of steel or other approved material, although restricted use of flexible pipes shall be permissible in positions where the Administration is satisfied that they are necessary.
rules.else_explanation: The rule also allows "other approved material" and restricted use of flexible pipes, but no approval is recorded in the model. Add the approval reference or use steel.

rules.source: ShipCheck data quality (internal check, not a regulation)
rules.clause: Design status VFI must be "Final" before a result is final
rules.text: Parts whose design status is not Final may still change; their check results are provisional.

rules.source: ShipCheck data quality (internal check, not a regulation)
rules.clause: Model fields must not hold "Error" or "---"
rules.text: A model field that holds "Error" or "---" cannot be used for a check; the part is reported for correction in the design tool.
